text.p: McDonald's Corp. said Wednesday it will decentralize its U.S. operations into five geographic divisions in an effort to move decision-making and accountability closer to the restaurant level.
McDonald's also said that Edward Rensi, who has been president and chief executive officer of McDonald's U.S.A., is retiring. The company cited personal family commitments.

"Ed Rensi has been by my side for more than 25 years, helping immeasurably to expand McDonald's into the world's largest food-service organisation and the best known brand," McDonald's Corp. Chairman Michael Quinlan said in a statement.
He said Rensi agreed to stay on as a consultant to help complete development of a new production system.
Jack Greenberg, chairman of McDonald's U.S.A., will assume the additional title of chief executive officer of its U.S. business.
As part of the management realignment, McDonald's will eliminate eight zone officer positions based in Oak Brook, Ill., to which its 40 U.S. operating regions previously reported.
Those regions will now report to the appropriate division presidents, McDonald's said.

The company, which has more than 21,000 restaurants worldwide and over 12,000 in the United States, said the division presidents will have full responsibility and accountability for the performance of their divisions.

By Sept. 1, the division presidents will appoint divisional management teams, including restaurant support operations. Divisional presidents will decide if and when their teams will relocate to the field, McDonald's said.
McDonald's stock gained 69 cents to 49.44 at midday on the New York Stock Exchange on the news.
Company franchisees had said in May that the fast-food giant was expected to reorganize its U.S. management.

The Northeast Division, headed by Alan Feldman, will encompass 2,210 restaurants; Southeast Division, headed by Debra Koenig, 2,820 restaurants; Great Lakes Division, headed by Kevin Dunn, 2,370 restaurants; Midwest Division, headed by John Charlesworth, 2,390 restaurants, and Western Division, headed by Michael Roberts, 2,310 restaurants.

"When Jack Greenberg was elected chairman of McDonald's USA last October, we decided there was a clear need to bring more focused management closer to our restaurants, with the goal of serving our customers better than ever before," Quinlan said. "This new structure addresses that need, and I'm confident we will be a stronger company for it."
Greenberg said division presidents will have the authority to innovate new approaches to meet business objectives, but must maintain a uniform commitment to McDonald's "basic principles."

"We want the 'line' -- which for McDonald's includes our divisional and regional staffs, owner/operators and restaurant personnel -- to make decisions on behalf of customers based on field operating needs," Greenberg said. "The line ultimately has responsibility and accountability for our business success."

McDonald's also said that Thomas Glasgow, executive vice president and chief operations officer, and Thomas Dentice, executive vice president, are changing their roles in the company and are expected to become U.S. owner/operators.
